reports.title: JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results

guidance.heading: Business Outlook
section: For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company expects net revenues to be between US$650 million and US$669 million. This forecast reflects the Company’s current and preliminary views on the market, operational conditions, and business strategies, which are subject to change, particularly as to the potential impact from macroeconomic uncertainties.

desk.headline: Revenue up 15.6% to $624.6m, beat; adjusted EPS $1.36 beat; Q4 revenue outlook $650–669m

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted, per ADS, continuing operations

results: Revenue rose 15.6% to $624.6m, with BIGO Ads up 39.6% and Shopline up 24.7%; live-streaming-led Social Entertainment grew 8.8%.
Non-live-streaming businesses now make up 32.8% of revenue, up from 28.1% a year ago.
GAAP operating income fell to $13.5m on higher costs, while adjusted operating income rose to $46.6m from $40.7m.
Adjusted net income fell to $67.1m from $72.4m; adjusted EPS held at $1.36 thanks to fewer shares.
Operating cash flow was $102.2m; $536.0m has gone back to shareholders this year, and a $1.59 per ADS dividend was declared.

guidance.summary: JOYY expects Q4 revenue of $650–669m, 11.7–14.9% growth. On the call it also lifted its 2026 growth target for third-party ad revenue to nearly 60% (from about 50%) and kept its target of about 20% growth in full-year adjusted operating income.

points: Q4 growth is expected in the mid-single digits for Social Entertainment and above 20% for Shopline.
No formal 2027 guidance yet, but management expects solid revenue growth and higher adjusted operating profit.
Longer-term targets: $1bn of third-party BIGO Ads revenue and operating break-even at Shopline, both in 2028.
BIGO Ads completed its link-up with Google AdMob Mediation in October; the contribution is still small.
Lower adjusted net income was blamed mainly on foreign-exchange losses; the finance head said the share price does not reflect the company's value.
call.source: Call coverage: Motley Fool call transcript, 19 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Whether Q4 revenue lands in the $650–669m range.
BIGO Ads growth and margins as third-party traffic costs rise.
Foreign-exchange losses and impairments hitting reported profit.
